model_annotation: This plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of several methods as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to about 5,000, with tick marks at 10⁰·⁷ (~5), 10¹, 10², 10³, and beyond. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 37% to 65%, with tick marks at intervals of 5 percentage points. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method. The "Base" line (black with circle markers, solid) starts at approximately 37% at the lowest co-occurrence number and rises slightly to around 43.5% at the highest, remaining relatively flat after the second data point. The "FT" line (light blue with downward-pointing triangle markers, solid) begins near 40% and increases to approximately 47.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "IKE" line (red with upward-pointing triangle markers, solid) starts at roughly 43% and rises to about 49% at the highest co-occurrence value. The "MEND" line (brown with diamond markers, solid) begins at approximately 44.5% and increases to around 56.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "MEMIT" line (purple with pentagon markers, solid) starts near 44% and rises to approximately 54.5% at the rightmost data point. The "ROME" line (green with square markers, solid) begins at roughly 51% at the lowest co-occurrence number and increases steadily to approximately 65.5% at the highest co-occurrence number, maintaining the highest values across the entire range. All lines show a generally increasing trend across the x-axis, though the rate and magnitude of increase vary among methods.
